title: Python SlotClaim: allocation_mode never validated — raw int constructs and silently serializes inverted
description: Codereview finding (ft5w correctness pass, reviewer kimi-k3), P3. SlotClaim.__post_init__ (python/src/lichen/gateway/slot_claim.py:171-221) validates every field except allocation_mode, and encode_claim_canonical (:343-347) maps ANY non-AllocationMode.INTERLEAVED value to CONTIGUOUS. AllocationMode is a plain Enum (not IntEnum), so SlotClaim(..., allocation_mode=0) constructs without error and serializes inverted (intent interleaved=0 -> wire contiguous=1). Rust gets this strictness at compile time (mode: AllocationMode type). Local-construction-only (decode always yields enum members; no wire adversary), but a silent intent-inversion trap for any local caller. Fix: isinstance check in __post_init__ rejecting non-AllocationMode values, or explicit else: raise in encode_claim_canonical. Pin with a construct test: allocation_mode=0 and allocation_mode='interleaved' raise ClaimError.
close_reason: Done. __post_init__ now requires isinstance(allocation_mode, AllocationMode); raw int 0/1, str, None raise ClaimError (previously constructed silently and serialized INVERTED — any non-INTERLEAVED value maps to wire CONTIGUOUS at encode_claim_canonical). Pins: construct test rejecting 4 bad types + accepting both enum members. 103 passed, 3 skipped. 1x delegated correctness review: PASS; reviewer-confirmed no existing non-enum callers. (Reviewer's noted truncated comment + over-indented return at slot_claim.py:530-531 is pre-existing from commit a3bf9e62a7, out of scope.)
